literal: At the place where it is effective, he who restrains anger is he who restrains. At the place where it is not, if restrained, what? If not restrained, what?
translation: He who restrains his anger where it can be effective is the true restrainer. Where it cannot be effective, what does it matter whether he restrains it or not?
modern: தன் சினம் பலிக்கும் இடத்தில் அதைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துபவனே உண்மையாகவே சினத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்துபவன் ஆவான். சினம் பலிக்காத இடத்தில், அதைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தினால் என்ன, கட்டுப்படுத்தாவிட்டால் என்ன?
explanation: This couplet defines true restraint of anger by examining the power dynamic between people. The word 'செல்லிடத்து' (where it goes or is effective) refers to situations where a person has the power to act on their anger, such as against the weak. Restraining anger in such situations is the only genuine restraint. In contrast, 'அல்லிடத்து' (where it is not effective) refers to situations where one is powerless. In those cases, holding back anger is merely a necessity, and whether one restrains it or not makes no practical difference.
